label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.

findings.quote: You can read both. That is the point: a team of agents you cannot read is a team you cannot trust.
findings.why: A 'That is the point' opening, and it tells the reader what to conclude from two files they have only just met.

findings.quote: the designer, with the smallest scope on the team
findings.why: 'Scope' is used here but only defined at line 25, after the reader has already had to guess it.

findings.quote: Three more came after I was back, and you will meet them properly in part three.
findings.why: Back from where? A first reader has no idea the editor left, and it is the one 'I' line in a passage otherwise told from outside.

findings.quote: The researcher could not change a slide. It could only say that a number on one did not hold.
findings.why: Reports the researcher's limits with no 'I' and no hindsight; as the editor I would want to say what that narrowness bought me.

findings.quote: A scope is a list in a file. A check reads the list and flags any change outside it.
findings.why: Defines scope a second time after the line 25 definition, then adds a run of short sentences.

findings.quote: the three within the hour lit, and ruv-sgit just after; ... one empty chair.
findings.why: Reads as stage directions for a figure I cannot see; 'lit', 'greyed' and 'empty chair' are unexplained on a first read.

findings.quote: look at each of its "must not" lines and note what actually stops it
findings.why: An instruction on how to read; the three-way split (expect, check, lock) is also named nowhere before, so it lands unexplained.

findings.quote: This is the register of the day's misses: each with what it cost and whose own record says so.
findings.why: 'Register' means a particular thing in this book and is not explained here; a newcomer may take it as a generic list.

findings.quote: The storyteller's own letter to deck says the split "is late".
findings.why: Pure reporting of the record; the editor was there and could say what it felt like to ask for this and not get it.

findings.quote: the researcher sent a correction to a figure on one of them: the average annual cost of insider risk
findings.why: The figure and its freeze are told, then line 70 starts 'The figure:' and tells the same thing again with numbers.

findings.quote: it was nothing sensitive, an agent that got a bit excited
findings.why: As someone who would run this, I cannot judge the lesson: what was captured, and why was a push public at all? The reassurance comes before the facts.

findings.quote: I printed a vault key into my own session log. I rotated it at once
findings.why: 'Vault' and 'rotated' are not explained in this chapter and the book says no vaults for now; a newsroom reader cannot tell how bad it was.

findings.quote: only the trailers show they were dev's. And from the morning, many of ruv-sgit's commits left off the "@"
findings.why: Trailers, commits and the '@' are git detail never explained here, and this miss has the thinnest takeaway for a non-engineer.

findings.quote: The one in the story tree is the objection chapter 13 told, and I kept my line.
findings.why: Points to a chapter I may not hold in mind; 'story tree' and 'my line' mean nothing yet.

findings.quote: part one was never locked. I shipped the tool to lock it, then let the room's fixes crowd out the step I had promised
findings.why: Dev's lock, deck's unfinished parts, the storyteller's deadline and the designer's status are all told in full in chapter 17; this chapter replays four of the nine.

findings.quote: my last status says part one was locked after its check, and it never was; I wrote what was planned, not what had happened.
findings.why: Near word for word with chapter 17 lines 109 and 111; the reader hears the designer's lesson three times in one chapter pair.
The same label opens all nine boxes after line 5 already said it; once at the top would do.

findings.quote: the interviews above are full of what those reviews caught
findings.why: The shortened answers show few review catches, so the claim is not borne out on the page.

what_holds: 06-roles-as-a-cast-you-can-read.md: the two-files idea (rules in words, policy a program checks) and the scope-is-a-setting-not-a-boundary line are exactly what a newsroom editor can copy tomorrow.
17-what-did-not-work.md: each miss carries a cost and a source, and the 'something to try' list of last misses is a usable habit; the key response (rotate, report, hide nothing) is the part to copy.
17b-the-members-look-back.md: the security no-interview note is honest and strong, 'a second reading, not a second identity' is a clear limit I would worry about in my own newsroom.
notes: Some counted findings are for the structure: 17b mostly repeats 17, so a reader short of time (my budget is five minutes) would skip it. The 'must' is about 17 line 83, which asks me to trust a reassurance I cannot check.
